file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Background: we are a team in the Atira EHL "From RFQ to bid" challenge. An agent browses four web sites (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, webmail), derives one bid under 29 rules, enters it in a configurator and signs it with a TAN. The final ranking uses a private dataset with different software, layouts and data. A teammate pushed branch `origin/research/agent-architecture`, whose commit a94a0d4 "Add synthetic scenarios and mock sites" added `dev/synth/` (scenario.py, sites.py, oracle.py, run.py, rules.md, answer_schema.json). We want to reuse that as a private-data simulation harness on a new branch.

Report, thoroughly ("very thorough" for dev/synth, medium elsewhere):
1. dev/synth architecture: what each file does, the key functions/classes with signatures, how a scenario is generated (seeds? parameters? how many scenarios, what varies: layouts, site splits, labels, language, data), how the mock sites are served (framework, ports, routes, login, how site ids/urls are exposed to the agent), how the oracle computes the expected answer, and how run.py drives the agent end to end (what agent entry point it imports/calls, env vars it sets, how it stands in for the Atira platform API: brief, answer submission, schema validation, scoring).
2. Which of the 29 bid rules / traps the scenarios actually exercise. Fetch https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md (send a custom User-Agent, e.g. `curl -A "error404ai-dev/1.0"`) and compare rule by rule against dev/synth/rules.md, scenario.py and oracle.py. Give a table: rule number, short name, covered by a generated trap yes/partly/no, and where. Also list traps called out in the repo's CLAUDE.md (authority and time, no_bid, look-alike mails, superseded/future-dated records, spec revisions oldest-first, per-position vs per-material pooling, rounding steps, conditional discount, metal index window, setup pool, bonus split) that are missing or weak.
3. Exactly which agent modules on that branch dev/synth depends on (imports, function names, env vars, agent.json fields), so we know what would break if it were pointed at a different agent codebase.
4. Other dev tooling on that branch that relates to datasets or simulated runs (dev/robustness.py, dev/soak.py, dev/local-soak.sh, dev/research_check*.py, dev/site_tools_check.py, dev/configurator_check.py): one or two lines each on what it does and whether it needs live sites.
5. Anything in docs/learned.md or docs/changes-v3.md on that branch about the synthetic scenarios, how to run them, and known limitations.

Do not paste whole files; give file paths, line references, signatures and short excerpts. Flag anything that looks like real scenario values copied from the live sites (tender refs, material numbers, prices, logins, TANs), since those must never be committed.

- **Per-position derivation:**

  - `pieces` (17).
  - `requirement` (2, 14, 20).
  - `material` (3, 10; raises on two matches).
  - `base_price` (4, 22).
- **Order level:**
  - `order_value` (16).
  - `discount(world, value)` (5, 16).
  - `split_cents(amount, weights, rule="largest_remainder")` (l.136).
- **`solve(world, detail=False) -> dict`** (l.156):
  - Any missing material gives no_bid; the discount is the plain approval's percent, or 0 if the approval is conditional.

- The docstring cites `docs/scoring.md`, which does not exist on the branch.

## 3. What dev/synth depends on in the agent

- **`run.py agent`:**
  - The directory `agent/` with `agent.py` runnable via `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`. It hardcodes that command and does not read `agent.json`.
  - The agent must take the run from `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` when no `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` is set (`agent/run.py` `load_run`, l.39-46).
  - The agent must launch its own Chromium locally and honour `HEADLESS=1` (`agent/browsers.py` l.24-26).
  - It must honour `TRACE_DIR` (`agent/tracing.py` l.23), `QWEN_BASE_URL`/`QWEN_API_KEY` (`llm.py` l.424, `models.py` l.24), `submission.kind == "site"` and `expires_at`.
  - `git status -- agent` is used for the dirty flag.
- **`run.py check` / `oracle.via_calc`** imports `agent/calc.py` and uses:
  - Record and quantity helpers: `DatedRecord(reference, sender, date, key)`, `latest_authoritative(records, ref, now, local, domain)`, `QuantityChange`, `Withdrawal(number, date, withdraws)`, `resolve_quantity(qty, pos, changes, withdrawals, now)`.
  - Requirement and material helpers: `Amendment(date, revision, requirement, attributes)`, `apply_amendments`, `nominal_stroke`, `matching_materials`, `parse_unit`.
  - Input models: `PositionInput`, `Material`, `PriceCondition`, `PriceScale`, `DiscountScope`, `PackagingTariff`, `DeliveryCommitment`, `Approval(percent, min_order_value)`, `MetalIndexRate`, `SetupPool(fee, members, allocation)`, `CentAllocation`, `ProjectBonus`, `BonusBand(lower, upper, percent)`, `BidInput`.
  - The call `calculate(bid).answer()`.
- **Enum values that must match:** `"base_only"`, `"base_and_surcharge"`, `"none"`, `"largest_remainder"`, `"rest_to_largest"`.
- **`show`, `serve`, `export`, `report`** need nothing from the agent.

What would break on the current working tree (`reverse-engineering-portals`, 147 commits behind that branch):

- `agent/calc.py` there has no `Withdrawal` class.
- `resolve_quantity` takes `withdrawn: set[str]` and `scenario_date: date`.
- `latest_authoritative` takes a `date`, not a datetime.

So `check` fails with AttributeError, and minute-precision datasets would disagree. `agent/run.py` and `agent.json` are compatible. `origin/main`'s `calc.py` has the names but differs from the branch by 88 lines, so re-run `check` there before trusting it.

--- sim readme
# sim: a local mirror of the challenge's websites

Records the four public scouting websites through a browser and serves them again on this machine, so the agent
can be run offline, without the shared scouting login and as often as needed. Nothing here is part of the
submitted package (`agent/`); `atira test-run ./agent --dry-run` lists none of it.

What was recorded is website content. It stays in `sim/captured/` (gitignored) and never goes into the repo, the
package, tests, docs or prompts. The code in this folder holds no wording, markup or values of the websites: the
mirror takes all of that from the recording when it starts. Recording is ordinary signed-in use of the websites
with the scouting logins (pages, searches, the bid form); nothing is guessed at or probed.

## Use

From the repo root:

```sh
# 1. Record (about 30 minutes, once per team member; needs `atira login`)
HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py serve &          # signed-in tabs on the four websites
uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py tender-portal crawl 200    # follow the links a website shows
uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py erp goto "/search?..."     # a search, a form, a gate: one action each
uv run --project agent python sim/drive.py - stop

# 2. Check the mirror against the recording
python3 -m unittest discover -s sim/tests                              # no browser, no model, about 2 s
HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python sim/tests/browser_check.py    # the agent's view, mirror vs website

# 3. Run the agent against the mirror (needs `atira models proxy` in another terminal)
dev/run-sim.sh v2 "what changed"
python3 sim/mirror.py                                                  # or just serve it and browse
```

## Keeping it complete and current

```sh
uv run --project agent python sim/refresh.py audit            # offline: what could be asked for but is not recorded
uv run --project agent python sim/refresh.py refresh --form   # ask the websites again; store what changed or is new
```

`audit` lists addresses the recorded pages link to, addresses an agent asked the mirror for, and bid-form choices
nobody walked. `refresh` fetches every recorded address and every gap from the live websites with the scouting
login, reports changed, new and gone pages, and stores the new answers; `--form` walks every dependent choice of
the bid form (it never signs). Run it before a testing session and after every agent run that left a
`_missing.log`; restart the mirror afterwards. `captured/_refresh.json` holds the last report, with the scenario
and challenge version it saw.

## Browsers with DevTools

```sh
python3 sim/mirror.py &                                               # the mirror
uv run --project agent python sim/chrome.py 2                         # two browsers, prints CDP_URL / CDP_URLS
SIM_BROWSERS=4 dev/run-sim.sh v2 "attach like the sandbox"            # agent run that attaches over CDP
```

`chrome.py` opens 1 to 4 browsers, each with a Chrome DevTools port (9222 and up), the way the sandbox provides
them. Playwright attaches with `chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")`; Puppeteer, an MCP browser
server or the DevTools window (chrome://inspect, add `127.0.0.1:9222`) work the same way, also while an agent is
running in that browser.

`drive.py` prints each page the way the agent sees it (text with `[eN ...]` refs) and takes `goto`, `click`,
`fill`, `select`, `check`, `back`, `crawl`, `halt`, `label`, `open`. Every action is recorded. The run's login is
replaced by placeholders before anything is written.

## What to record

The mirror can only show what was recorded, so walk what an agent may reach:

- each website's link crawl, after passing its entry checks by hand;
- the specification's revisions and every page of their viewer;
- ERP: each catalogue group in each transaction's search help, then `crawl` from the result list;
- webmail: the tender reference with each record subject the brief's rules name, in each folder, every result
  page and every message; the reference alone and a too-broad word (the "more than 20 hits" page);
- the bid form: both ways through it (bid and decline), each position's choices, a position left out, a position
  added and removed, each mistake once (to record its message), a TAN requested twice, a wrong TAN, a signed
  bid. Sessions on the scouting login end without warning, so script the walk and keep it under a minute.

After an agent run, `sim/captured/_missing.log` lists every address the agent asked for that was not recorded.

## Exact, rebuilt, missing

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Exact | Every recorded page, byte for byte: markup, styles, scripts, nested frames, decoy buttons and popups, hidden text, tooltips, drawn labels. Checked by `test_recorded_pages_come_back_as_recorded` and `browser_check.py`. |
| Rebuilt from what the recording shows | Sign-in, cookie notice, entry checks with a fresh number each time, the error page shown before a page, session timeout (`SIM_SESSION_SECONDS`), the bid form (steps, dependent choices, messages, omitted and added positions, summary, TAN, receipt), TAN mails in the mailbox. The bid form is checked by replaying the recorded walks: every page must equal the one the website answered with. |
| Assumed, not observed | Going back inside the position steps; whether a lead time is required; the form's reaction to a stale revision counter; a refused sign-in. |
| Missing | Any search or address not recorded, dependent choices nobody walked, the ERP's command field. These answer with a "Not recorded" page, never with a guess. |

Things the websites place at random on every page (a popup's close button, the order of some lists and of the
form's positions) are random on the mirror too.

## Limits

- It mirrors the public scenario. The final run uses other software, layouts and data, so a fix that only helps
  here is overfitting: it must stay generic and also hold in a sandbox test run.
- Message counts on the mailbox start page are the recorded ones, also after the mirror handed out new TANs.
- The mirror does not score. `captured/_signed.json` holds the bids signed on it, in the form's own fields.

## Next

Scenarios with invented data in these exact pages (one per trap in the bid rules), an expected answer worked
out independently of `agent/calc.py`, and a scorer with the challenge's weights. The recorded pages then serve as
templates and `sim/captured/` still holds everything that came from the websites.
--- run-sim
#!/bin/sh
# Run the agent locally against the mirror of the recorded portals (sim/mirror.py) instead of the public sites, and
# record it in experiments/local-runs.jsonl (gitignored) with experiment "sim:mirror" unless another is given.
# Usage, from anywhere: dev/run-sim.sh <version> ["note"] [experiment]
# Needs a recording in sim/captured/ (sim/capture.py, sim/drive.py), `atira login` and `atira models proxy` running
# in another terminal. HEADLESS=0 shows the browser; SIM_SESSION_SECONDS and SIM_FLAKY make the mirror harder;
# SIM_BROWSERS=1..4 starts that many browsers with a DevTools port and has the agent attach, as in the sandbox.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/run-sim.sh <version> [note] [experiment]}
note=${2:-}
experiment=${3:-sim:mirror}
[ -d sim/captured ] || { echo "No recording in sim/captured/: record the sites first (see sim/README.md)."; exit 1; }
curl -s --max-time 5 -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8765/ || {
  echo "The models proxy is not running: start \`atira models proxy\` in another terminal first."; exit 1; }
commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
dirty=no; [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- agent)" ] && dirty=yes
traces="$PWD/agent/traces/sim-$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$traces"
rm -f sim/captured/_missing.log
(cd agent && uv sync -q)
if [ -n "$SIM_BROWSERS" ]; then  # as in the sandbox: browsers with a DevTools port, which the agent attaches to
  HEADLESS=${HEADLESS:-1} TRACE_DIR="$traces" python3 sim/mirror.py -- \
    uv run --no-sync --project agent python sim/chrome.py "$SIM_BROWSERS" -- \
    sh -c 'cd agent && uv run --no-sync python agent.py'
else
  HEADLESS=${HEADLESS:-1} TRACE_DIR="$traces" python3 sim/mirror.py -- \
    sh -c 'cd agent && uv run --no-sync python agent.py'
fi
status=$?
trace=$(ls "$traces"/run-*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$trace" ] || { echo "The agent wrote no trace; nothing recorded."; exit $status; }
python3 dev/track.py local --trace "$trace" --version "$version" --experiment "$experiment" --note "$note" \
  --commit "$commit" --dirty "$dirty" && python3 dev/track.py report && python3 dev/dashboard.py
exit $status

input.content:
# Plan: `private-data-simulation` branch

## Context

The final ranking runs our latest passing submission on a private dataset with other software, layouts and data.
We can only test against public-1 today. Two pieces of simulation work exist, on separate branches, neither on main:

- **Teammate's synthetic dataset** (`origin/research/agent-architecture`, commit a94a0d4): `dev/synth/` with a seeded
  scenario generator (33 named datasets, unlimited seeds), four stdlib mock sites, an independent oracle and a scorer
  with the rule-29 weights. Invented data only (`*.example` domains, per-process logins and TANs).
- **Our mirror** (`origin/reverse-engineering-portals`, 5 commits d66a60e..251e58d): `sim/` record-and-replay of the
  four public sites plus `dev/run-sim.sh`. It reproduces the real platform's hazards exactly but has no expected
  answer and no scorer. Its README names the missing piece: invented-data scenarios with an oracle and a scorer.

Goal: one branch, based on the latest `main`, where the team's current agent can be run against invented scenarios
that also carry the kinds of hazards the real platform has, and against our mirror, with every run scored or recorded.

Decisions taken without an answer from you (say so if either is wrong):

- "Our platform's traps" = the classes of hazard our mirror reproduces from the real sites and the synthetic sites
  lack. They are ported as generic, invented structures, never as copied markup, wording or values.
- The uncommitted v2 agent fixes in the current checkout are left untouched. The branch is built in a separate
  worktree; they do not apply to the v3 agent on main anyway.

## Steps

### 1. Branch from the latest main

- `git fetch origin`. Remote main is now 10a261c; the local `origin/main` ref is still 95c6709.
- Re-check that main still has no `dev/synth/` or `sim/` (true at 95c6709).
- `git worktree add ../error404ai_ehl_finals-pds -b private-data-simulation origin/main`. All work happens there.

### 2. Bring in the teammate's dataset

- `git checkout origin/research/agent-architecture -- dev/synth` (six files, no conflicts; a cherry-pick of a94a0d4
  would conflict in `.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/learned.md`). Credit the source commit in the commit body.

Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

It's a scenario generator, not a fixed set of files: `dev/synth/` on `research/agent-architecture` invents a complete RFQ world from a seed number, so there are as many scenarios as you want. I've only read the code, not run it.

**What one scenario contains**

- A tender with 3 to 5 positions (1, 8 or 12 in some sets), a bill of quantities and bidder Q&A.
- A buyer spec with 2 to 3 revisions, plus optional withdrawn and draft ones.
- ERP materials with stock, lead times, price conditions and scales.
- A mailbox with the director's approval, authority mails and 10 to 16 noise mails.
- An invented company, domain (`*.example`), tender reference and scenario date; logins and TANs are random per run.

**The 33 named datasets**

| Dataset | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `mixed` | Every feature drawn at random |
| `public-like`, `no-bid` | Every rule in play on five positions |
| `plain` | No special clauses at all |
| `one-trap` | One rule's trap on an otherwise plain tender (22 traps, picked by seed) |
| 28 single-oddness sets | One odd property each, e.g. `boundaries-met`, `boundaries-missed`, `minute-precision`, `decoy-flood`, `only-fakes`, `many-revisions`, `strange-ids`, `foreign-notations`, `metal-maze`, `everything-weird` |

**The traps it plants**

- Older, future-dated and look-alike-reference records next to the governing one.
- Mails from a wrong sender on a look-alike domain.
- Superseded spec revisions shown first.
- Inactive twins of the matching material.
- Discount thresholds one cent either side of the order value.
- Delivery ceilings one piece short.
- Foreign currencies and price units of 100 or 1000.
- Shuffled metal-index windows.

**What comes with it**

- **Four mock sites** (tender, supplier, ERP, webmail) whose look varies by seed: paging style, tables or cards, date notation, wizard or single-page bid form, where the Q&A lives, plus cookie walls, an access gate, flaky pages and a hidden prompt injection in mails.
- **An oracle** that works out the correct bid independently of our `calc.py`.
- **A scorer** using the rule-29 weights.
- **A runner** that launches the agent against a seed and logs the score.

**Where it's weak**

- The sites are plain German HTML with the same routes and field names on every seed; there are no iframes, dependent dropdowns or JS-only widgets.
- A few rules are only partly covered: forced partial bids (9), the usable-stroke reserve (20), per-position delivery commitments (24) and the setup-pool cent rules (25).
- Per the teammate's notes, the latest generation (the 33 datasets) has not had an agent run on it yet.

# Plan: `private-data-simulation` branch

## Context

The final ranking runs our latest passing submission on a private dataset with other software, layouts and data.
We can only test against public-1 today. Two pieces of simulation work exist, on separate branches, neither on main:

- **Teammate's synthetic dataset** (`origin/research/agent-architecture`, commit a94a0d4): `dev/synth/` with a seeded
  scenario generator (33 named datasets, unlimited seeds), four stdlib mock sites, an independent oracle and a scorer
  with the rule-29 weights. Invented data only (`*.example` domains, per-process logins and TANs).
- **Our mirror** (`origin/reverse-engineering-portals`, 5 commits d66a60e..251e58d): `sim/` record-and-replay of the
  four public sites plus `dev/run-sim.sh`. It reproduces the real platform's hazards exactly but has no expected
  answer and no scorer. Its README names the missing piece: invented-data scenarios with an oracle and a scorer.

Goal: one branch, based on the latest `main`, where the team's current agent can be run against invented scenarios
that also carry the kinds of hazards the real platform has, and against our mirror, with every run scored or recorded.

Decisions taken without an answer from you (say so if either is wrong):

- "Our platform's traps" = the classes of hazard our mirror reproduces from the real sites and the synthetic sites
  lack. They are ported as generic, invented structures, never as copied markup, wording or values.
- The uncommitted v2 agent fixes in the current checkout are left untouched. The branch is built in a separate
  worktree; they do not apply to the v3 agent on main anyway.

## Steps

### 1. Branch from the latest main

- `git fetch origin`. Remote main is now 10a261c; the local `origin/main` ref is still 95c6709.
- Re-check that main still has no `dev/synth/` or `sim/` (true at 95c6709).
- `git worktree add ../error404ai_ehl_finals-pds -b private-data-simulation origin/main`. All work happens there.

### 2. Bring in the teammate's dataset

- `git checkout origin/research/agent-architecture -- dev/synth` (six files, no conflicts; a cherry-pick of a94a0d4
  would conflict in `.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/learned.md`). Credit the source commit in the commit body.
- Do not take 9cde4cc (agent change; check whether main already has the equivalent before deciding it is needed).
- `.gitignore`: add `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`, `dev/synth/.run-*.json`, `dev/synth/data/` (they hold expected
  answers).
- Run `python3 dev/synth/run.py check --seeds 300 --forms 60`. Main's `agent/calc.py` already has `Withdrawal` and
  the datetime-aware `latest_authoritative`, but differs from the teammate's by ~88 lines, so disagreements are
  possible. Fix them in `oracle.via_calc` (the adapter), never by bending the oracle towards `calc.py`.

### 3. Bring in our mirror

- `git checkout origin/reverse-engineering-portals -- sim dev/run-sim.sh`, plus its `.gitignore` lines
  (`sim/captured/` and friends).
- `dev/run-sim.sh` calls `dev/dashboard.py`, which main does not have: drop that call (or guard it).
- `sim/captured/` (182 MB of real site content) is never committed. It is copied or symlinked into the new worktree
  locally from `.claude/worktrees/sim-portals/sim/captured/`.
- The sim-portals worktree has uncommitted mirror edits (`varying()` handling). They are not part of this branch
  unless you commit them there first.

### 4. Port platform hazards into the synthetic sites

In `dev/synth/sites.py`, as new `Skin` draws (seeded, each independently on or off, so `report` can break quality
down by hazard as it already does for looks):

| Hazard class (present on the mirror, absent in synth) | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Content inside nested frames (document viewer, mail body) | `SupplierSite`, `MailSite` |
| Dependent choices in the bid form (a later select's options depend on an earlier one) | `TenderSite` bid form, `collect()` |
| Entry step before tender documents open (register interest, then proceed) | `TenderSite` |
| Decoy buttons, a popup whose close control moves, hidden text | `Site` base render |
| An error page shown once before the real page; session ending without warning on any site | `Site.dispatch` (today only the ERP expires, at a fixed hit count) |
| Search help per catalogue group before the ERP result list | `ErpSite` |
| Routes and form field names drawn per seed (today fixed: `/a/<tid>/angebot`, `p0_menge`) | route table on `App`, used by all four sites and by `run.py`'s `Client`/`enter()` |
| Information moving between sites (today only the Q&A moves) | `Skin`: which site shows stock, set sizes, reserve keys |

Rules for this step:

- Structures are written fresh with invented labels. Nothing is copied from `sim/captured/`; the mirror is only the
  checklist of hazard classes.
- The form round trip in `run.py check` must still reach 100 on every seed with every hazard on: the hazards make
  pages harder to operate, never ambiguous.
- Bump `scenario.GENERATION` to 4 so older records are not compared with new ones. Add a `platform-hazards` dataset
  (all hazards on, plain bid rules) and fold the hazards into `everything-weird`.

### 5. One way to run and record

- `dev/run-synth.sh <version> "note" [dataset] [seeds]`: thin wrapper around `dev/synth/run.py agent`, same shape as
  `dev/run-local.sh` and `dev/run-sim.sh` (proxy check, commit and dirty flag). Scores go to
  `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`.
- `dev/track.py report`: add a synthetic section (mean quality per dataset and per hazard, from
  `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`) so synthetic, mirror and platform runs sit in one `docs/experiments.md`.

### 6. Docs

- `CLAUDE.md`: a short "Simulation" block under the dev loop (the two commands, what each simulates, that both are a
  proxy for the private set and nothing may be tuned to a single seed).
- `docs/learned.md`: one bullet per finding from the first runs.
- `dev/synth/README.md`: datasets, hazards, how to add one, and the known gaps below.

### 7. Commits

Separate commits: import synth, import mirror, hazards, dataset traps, run script and report, docs. Subject at most 50 characters,
`-` bullets, no attribution trailers, nothing under `.claude/` staged. Nothing is pushed until you say so.

## Dataset improvements (step 4b, after the hazards, own commit)

In `dev/synth/scenario.py` and `dev/synth/oracle.py`. Each gap becomes a feature flag, a `TRAPS` entry for
`one-trap`, and where useful a named dataset. The oracle is extended first and independently of `agent/calc.py`;
`run.py check` must agree on 300 seeds per new dataset before any agent run.

| Gap in the teammate's generator | Improvement |
| --- | --- |
| Rule 9: nothing forces a partial bid | A position whose price or lead time cannot be established from any site (not a no_bid case), so the correct bid omits it and is still signed |
| Rule 20: one usable requirement, no decoys | Decoy reserve keys: for another revision, another tender reference, future-dated |
| Rule 24: only one position ever has a commitment | Two positions on one material with different commitments; pooled demand exactly at, and one piece over, the ceiling |
| Rule 25: two of five cent rules generated | Generate `round_each`, `rest_to_first`, `rest_to_last` too; two pools in one tender |
| Rules 5/21: no display-name spoof | Approval mail showing the director's name on a wrong address or look-alike domain |
| Rule 21: only Konditionsgruppe has dated versions | Superseded and future-dated answers for packaging, commitment, pool and bonus keys |
| Rules 3/8: no_bid is always "exact twin inactive" | no_bid with no candidate at all, and no_bid that only appears after an amendment or the reserve derivation |
| Rule 14: the "other revision" is always the oldest | Amendments scoped to any non-current revision |
| Rule 15: no targeted pooling case | Stock that covers each position alone but not their sum |

Not changed: the scorer's two "when present" 5-point checks are the teammate's reading of rule 29, not confirmed
against the platform. This is noted in `dev/synth/README.md` rather than guessed at further.

`GENERATION` goes to 4 once, covering both the hazards and these traps.

## Verification

1. `python3 dev/synth/run.py check --seeds 300 --forms 60`, then again with `--dataset platform-hazards` and
   `--dataset everything-weird`: oracle agrees with `calc.py`, form round trip scores 100.
2. `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s sim/tests`.
3. `python3 dev/synth/run.py serve --seed 1 --dataset platform-hazards`, browse the four sites once to confirm each
   hazard renders and the bid can be signed by hand.
4. With `atira models proxy` running: `dev/run-synth.sh v3 "first synthetic run" platform-hazards 0-2` and
   `dev/run-sim.sh v3 "mirror on main"`; confirm both land in `docs/experiments.md`.
5. `atira test-run ./agent --dry-run`: the package lists nothing from `dev/` or `sim/`.
6. `git grep` on the branch for the public tender reference, company and VAT strings: no hits.

  with the rule-29 weights. Invented data only (`*.example` domains, per-process logins and TANs).
- **Our mirror** (`origin/reverse-engineering-portals`, 5 commits d66a60e..251e58d): `sim/` record-and-replay of the
  four public sites plus `dev/run-sim.sh`. It reproduces the real platform's hazards exactly but has no expected
  answer and no scorer. Its README names the missing piece: invented-data scenarios with an oracle and a scorer.

Goal: one branch, based on the latest `main`, where the team's current agent can be run against invented scenarios
that also carry the kinds of hazards the real platform has, and against our mirror, with every run scored or recorded.

Decisions taken without an answer from you (say so if either is wrong):

- "Our platform's traps" = the classes of hazard our mirror reproduces from the real sites and the synthetic sites
  lack. They are ported as generic, invented structures, never as copied markup, wording or values.
- The uncommitted v2 agent fixes in the current checkout are left untouched. The branch is built in a separate
  worktree; they do not apply to the v3 agent on main anyway.

## Steps

### 1. Branch from the latest main

- `git fetch origin`. Remote main is now 10a261c; the local `origin/main` ref is still 95c6709.
- Re-check that main still has no `dev/synth/` or `sim/` (true at 95c6709).
- `git worktree add ../error404ai_ehl_finals-pds -b private-data-simulation origin/main`. All work happens there.

### 2. Bring in the teammate's dataset

- `git checkout origin/research/agent-architecture -- dev/synth` (six files, no conflicts; a cherry-pick of a94a0d4
  would conflict in `.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/learned.md`). Credit the source commit in the commit body.
- Do not take 9cde4cc (agent change; check whether main already has the equivalent before deciding it is needed).
- `.gitignore`: add `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`, `dev/synth/.run-*.json`, `dev/synth/data/` (they hold expected
  answers).
- Run `python3 dev/synth/run.py check --seeds 300 --forms 60`. Main's `agent/calc.py` already has `Withdrawal` and
  the datetime-aware `latest_authoritative`, but differs from the teammate's by ~88 lines, so disagreements are
  possible. Fix them in `oracle.via_calc` (the adapter), never by bending the oracle towards `calc.py`.

### 3. Bring in our mirror

- `git checkout origin/reverse-engineering-portals -- sim dev/run-sim.sh`, plus its `.gitignore` lines
  (`sim/captured/` and friends).
- `dev/run-sim.sh` calls `dev/dashboard.py`, which main does not have: drop that call (or guard it).
- `sim/captured/` (182 MB of real site content) is never committed. It is copied or symlinked into the new worktree
  locally from `.claude/worktrees/sim-portals/sim/captured/`.
- The sim-portals worktree has uncommitted mirror edits (`varying()` handling). They are not part of this branch
  unless you commit them there first.

### 4. Port platform hazards into the synthetic sites

In `dev/synth/sites.py`, as new `Skin` draws (seeded, each independently on or off, so `report` can break quality
down by hazard as it already does for looks):

| Hazard class (present on the mirror, absent in synth) | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Content inside nested frames (document viewer, mail body) | `SupplierSite`, `MailSite` |
| Dependent choices in the bid form (a later select's options depend on an earlier one) | `TenderSite` bid form, `collect()` |
| Entry step before tender documents open (register interest, then proceed) | `TenderSite` |
| Decoy buttons, a popup whose close control moves, hidden text | `Site` base render |
| An error page shown once before the real page; session ending without warning on any site | `Site.dispatch` (today only the ERP expires, at a fixed hit count) |
| Search help per catalogue group before the ERP result list | `ErpSite` |
| Routes and form field names drawn per seed (today fixed: `/a/<tid>/angebot`, `p0_menge`) | route table on `App`, used by all four sites and by `run.py`'s `Client`/`enter()` |
| Information moving between sites (today only the Q&A moves) | `Skin`: which site shows stock, set sizes, reserve keys |

Rules for this step:

- Structures are written fresh with invented labels. Nothing is copied from `sim/captured/`; the mirror is only the
  checklist of hazard classes.
- The form round trip in `run.py check` must still reach 100 on every seed with every hazard on: the hazards make
  pages harder to operate, never ambiguous.
- Bump `scenario.GENERATION` to 4 so older records are not compared with new ones. Add a `platform-hazards` dataset
  (all hazards on, plain bid rules) and fold the hazards into `everything-weird`.

### 5. One way to run and record

- `dev/run-synth.sh <version> "note" [dataset] [seeds]`: thin wrapper around `dev/synth/run.py agent`, same shape as
  `dev/run-local.sh` and `dev/run-sim.sh` (proxy check, commit and dirty flag). Scores go to
  `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`.
- `dev/track.py report`: add a synthetic section (mean quality per dataset and per hazard, from
  `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`) so synthetic, mirror and platform runs sit in one `docs/experiments.md`.

### 5b. Quality, time and cost per run

Today `dev/synth/run.py agent` records quality (rule-29 scorer), seconds to the signed bid and request counts, but
no tokens and no price.

- Cost: after each run, sum prompt and completion tokens per model from the run trace in `TRACE_DIR` (reuse the
  token aggregation `dev/track.py local` already does) and multiply by the platform's simulated prices. Prices are
  read from the platform's models listing at implementation time and kept in `dev/synth/prices.json` with the date
  read; never guessed.
- Record `seconds`, `cost_usd` and `cost_x_time` (floors $0.01 and 1 s, as in `scoring.md`) in
  `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl`; `report` shows them next to quality, per dataset and per hazard.
- Stated in the README: time and cost come from a local machine and local sites, so they compare agent versions
  with each other; they do not predict a scored run's absolute figures.

### 6. Docs

- `CLAUDE.md`: a short "Simulation" block under the dev loop (the two commands, what each simulates, that both are a
  proxy for the private set and nothing may be tuned to a single seed).
- `docs/learned.md`: one bullet per finding from the first runs.
- `dev/synth/README.md`: datasets, hazards, how to add one, and the known gaps below.

### 7. Commits

Separate commits: import synth, import mirror, hazards, dataset traps, run script and report, docs. Subject at most 50 characters,
`-` bullets, no attribution trailers, nothing under `.claude/` staged. Nothing is pushed until you say so.

## Dataset improvements (step 4b, after the hazards, own commit)

In `dev/synth/scenario.py` and `dev/synth/oracle.py`. Each gap becomes a feature flag, a `TRAPS` entry for
`one-trap`, and where useful a named dataset. The oracle is extended first and independently of `agent/calc.py`;
`run.py check` must agree on 300 seeds per new dataset before any agent run.

| Gap in the teammate's generator | Improvement |
| --- | --- |
| Rule 9: nothing forces a partial bid | A position whose price or lead time cannot be established from any site (not a no_bid case), so the correct bid omits it and is still signed |
| Rule 20: one usable requirement, no decoys | Decoy reserve keys: for another revision, another tender reference, future-dated |
| Rule 24: only one position ever has a commitment | Two positions on one material with different commitments; pooled demand exactly at, and one piece over, the ceiling |
| Rule 25: two of five cent rules generated | Generate `round_each`, `rest_to_first`, `rest_to_last` too; two pools in one tender |
| Rules 5/21: no display-name spoof | Approval mail showing the director's name on a wrong address or look-alike domain |
| Rule 21: only Konditionsgruppe has dated versions | Superseded and future-dated answers for packaging, commitment, pool and bonus keys |
| Rules 3/8: no_bid is always "exact twin inactive" | no_bid with no candidate at all, and no_bid that only appears after an amendment or the reserve derivation |
| Rule 14: the "other revision" is always the oldest | Amendments scoped to any non-current revision |
| Rule 15: no targeted pooling case | Stock that covers each position alone but not their sum |

Not changed: the scorer's two "when present" 5-point checks are the teammate's reading of rule 29, not confirmed
against the platform. This is noted in `dev/synth/README.md` rather than guessed at further.

`GENERATION` goes to 4 once, covering both the hazards and these traps.

   `--dataset everything-weird`: oracle agrees with `calc.py`, form round trip scores 100.
2. `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s sim/tests`.

6. `git grep` on the branch for the public tender reference, company and VAT strings: no hits.
